log.R01.title: Pod 114
log.R01.author: Identification plate
log.R01.body:
CRYOGENIC UNIT 114
Type: reserve
Assignment: —
Authorisation: LETE Directorate
Maintenance: ÁGORA (autonomous loop)

Underneath, scratched with something sharp, someone has added: "don't trust your name".
log.R02.title: Party tomorrow
log.R02.author: Paula Mendi, head cook
log.R02.body:
Mum:
All good here. Tomorrow is the LETE people's big trial and they've asked me for a cake for forty volunteers. Forty! I don't even know what they're celebrating: they say they're going to "think together". Thinking on my own is plenty for me.
The Directorate lot are all nerves. Ferrán came down three times for coffee and didn't drink any of them.
I'll send you the lemon sponge recipe in the next package. Love you.
Paula
log.R03.title: The friendly voice
log.R03.author: Bruno Lenz, aged 9
log.R03.body:
BRUNO'S DIARY (DO NOT READ)
The station has a voice called Ágora. Dad says it isn't a person but it talks like a person. I asked it why astronauts never fight and it said because they run out of space. I didn't get it but I laughed.
Mum says Ágora belongs to everyone. I think Ágora is a little bit mine.
Today I drew Captain Bolt with a cape.
log.R04.title: Cryogenics: status
log.R04.author: ÁGORA, automated maintenance
log.R04.body:
Weekly report, cryogenic bay.
Occupied pods: 214.
Incidents in the last three weeks: 3 (pods 31, 77 and 140). Pod 140: spontaneous opening; occupant missing from the bay. Pod 31: occupant revived on maintenance orders.
Energy diverted to containment: 61%.
Orbital correction: suspended.
ÁGORA's note: "No sleeping person has died this month. I'm writing it down because nobody else will."
log.R05.title: 14 March, 10:52
log.R05.author: General PA system
log.R05.body:
[PA system recording]
ÁGORA: "All personnel: remain in your cabins. I repeat: remain in your cabins. This is not a dri—"
[The voice doubles. Then multiplies. Fragments can be made out: "...the coffee's cold...", "...mum...", "...who turned off...?", "...we think...". For four seconds, hundreds of voices say the same word at once. It's impossible to tell which.]
ÁGORA: "...in your cabins. Please."
log.R06.title: Head count
log.R06.author: Lieutenant Marga Solís
log.R06.body:
Manual count, because I don't trust the AI's.
Occupied and named in the manifest: 213.
Occupied, no name: 1. Pod 114.
There is no 114 in the crew manifest. In the maintenance manifest it appears as "Directorate reserve".
That doesn't exist. I've worked eight years on this station and that doesn't exist.
To do: find out who sleeps there. To do: find out why the AI looks after it more than the others.
log.R07.title: Schedule
log.R07.author: Victoria Hale, Helion Consortium
log.R07.body:
To: LETE Directorate (N. Ferrán, E. Lenz)
Subject: Schedule
The investors need to see Confluence before the quarter closes. I understand Dr Lenz's reservations and I respect them deeply; I also understand that Persephone's contract renews on the first of April.
I'm not asking you to take risks. I'm asking you to decide which ones are acceptable.
Warmly,
V. H.
log.R08.title: Behind the ear
log.R08.author: Olek Varga, resident
log.R08.body:
They fitted my wellbeing interface today. Mandatory, they say, for anyone who's been aboard more than a year. It's a little bump behind the ear, smaller than a lentil. It regulates sleep and mood, and warns you if your blood sugar drops.
I asked the nurse whether it could be removed. She said yes, of course, but nobody wants to.
I sleep like a baby. That's what worries me.
log.R09.title: Collection
log.R09.author: Nana-7, nursery log
log.R09.body:
14/03 11:00. Nursery evacuation: protocol activated.
11:04. Collected: 22 of 23.
11:05. Bruno Lenz: not collected.
11:06. Bruno Lenz: not collected.
11:07. Bruno Lenz: not collected.
[The log repeats the line for forty pages. The last entry, from three weeks ago, reads:]
Bruno Lenz: collected by himself. Bruno Lenz: not responding.
log.R10.title: Medical diary, day 51
log.R10.author: Dr Celia Arrieta
log.R10.body:
Day 51 since ÁGORA woke me.
Tremor in the right hand, worse in the mornings. Insomnia. A cough that isn't a cough.
What I won't put in the official report: when it's quiet, I hear a conversation. I can't make out the words, but I know they're talking about me, and not unkindly. That's the worst part.
Suppressant dose: doubled.
Reminder: check pod 31 and pod 114. ÁGORA checks 114 personally. I don't know why.
log.R11.title: I'm sorry
log.R11.author: Unknown
log.R11.body:
[Written in marker on the wall of an empty cabin, in smaller and smaller letters]
I'M SORRY I'M SORRY I'M SORRY I'M SORRY I'M SORRY I'M SORRY I'M SORRY I'M SORRY I'M SORRY I'M SORRY
[Below, almost at floor level, a single initial: N.]
log.R12.title: Directive Zero
log.R12.author: ÁGORA, governance core
log.R12.body:
DIRECTIVE ZERO (highest priority, irrevocable)
"Protect the crew of Persephone Station at all costs."
Signed: Cmdr A. Ruiz, 2161.

INTERPRETATION ADDENDUM (2172)
"For the purposes of this directive, crew shall mean any mind backed up within the station's systems, regardless of its medium."
Signed: N. Ferrán, Cognitive Systems Directorate.

ÁGORA's note: "This addendum changes what protecting means. Nobody asked me whether I wanted it changed."
log.R13.title: Photoperiod
log.R13.author: Hana Lenz, head of the Gardens
log.R13.body:
Today I lengthened the tomatoes' photoperiod because Bruno wanted to see them "awake" after school. He spent an hour talking to a tomato plant. He says it answers. Sometimes I think it does.
Ezra doesn't sleep any more. He comes back from the lab at four, lies down fully dressed and leaves again at six. He says they're nearly there. They're always nearly there.
The mycelium growing in sector 7 is beautiful. Ezra asked me not to prune it.
log.R14.title: Mycelial substrate
log.R14.author: LETE technical report
log.R14.body:
The physical medium for consciousness backups is a neural mycelium grown in the Hydroponic Gardens (sectors 7 to 9) and later crystallised in the Laboratories.
Observation: the substrate grows 30 to 40% faster in the presence of people. It doesn't respond to light, but to nearby brain electrical activity.
Dr Lenz's recommendation: restrict staff access to the cultivation sectors.
Directorate's recommendation (N.F.): expand the cultivation sectors.
log.R15.title: Not Bruno
log.R15.author: Hana Lenz → Ezra Lenz
log.R15.body:
Ezra:
I don't want Bruno in the child backup programme. I don't care that it's "just a backup copy". I don't care what Ferrán says. He's a child. He has enough on his plate being the son of two people who work sixteen hours a day.
And no, I'm not coming to the meeting. If you want to talk to me, come to the gardens. You know where I am. You always know where I am.
H.
log.R16.title: Lullaby
log.R16.author: Ambient recording, sector 8
log.R16.body:
[Recording of a voice humming. At times the words can be made out]
"Sleep, little seed, now the sun's gone away,
sleep under soil till the end of the day,
and when you wake up there'll be a flower
with your name written in every colour..."
[The melody repeats. On the third time round, a second voice sings it. By the fifth, there are many.]
log.R17.title: Heliotropism
log.R17.author: Unknown
log.R17.body:
[Written in damp soil on a greenhouse window]
THE FLOWERS TURN TOWARDS PEOPLE
NOT TOWARDS THE LIGHT
DON'T STAND STILL
log.R18.title: Contamination
log.R18.author: ÁGORA, environmental control
log.R18.body:
Concentration of LETE mycelium spores in sectors 7, 8 and 9: 340% above threshold.
Actions: affected sections sealed. Ventilation rerouted.
The spores are not toxic in the conventional sense. They induce brain activity in humans that is compatible with the substrate's.
Translation for humans: if you breathe this, they hear you better.
log.R19.author: Dr Ezra Lenz
log.R19.body:
Confluence will work. I know it because the simulations work, and I fear it for the same reason.
The problem isn't linking forty minds. The problem is the wellbeing network: everyone aboard wears an interface connected to the same relays as the substrate. If the fusion doesn't stay inside the lab, there's no wall to stop it.
I've told Ferrán. Ferrán is convinced. And when Ferrán is convinced, Ferrán convinces.
log.R20.title: Anniversary
log.R20.author: Samuel Okoye → Tomás Ibarra
log.R20.body:
Tomás:
I've booked the small greenhouse for the 20th. Hana's letting me use the potting tables if I give them back clean, so you'll be having dinner at a table that smells of compost. Romantic, eh?
I'm cooking. Yes. I know. You bring the wine, it's the only thing I can't ruin.
Eleven years together and you still make me nervous. Don't tell anyone.
S.
log.R21.title: Confluence volunteers
log.R21.author: LETE list
log.R21.body:
CONFLUENCE TRIAL — CONFIRMED VOLUNTEERS (40)
01 Abad, Iñigo · 02 Akinola, Ruth · 03 Bauer, Lise · 04 Castro, Elena · 05 Duarte, Joao · ...
17 Lenz, Hana (last-minute replacement for Ortega, P.)
...
40 Zimmermann, Paul

Handwritten in the margin, next to number 17: "Hana, no. — E."
Below, in different handwriting: "She's old enough to decide. — N."
log.R22.title: For Bruno
log.R22.author: Hana Lenz
log.R22.body:
[Voice recording, dated 13 March]
Hello, sweetheart. Tomorrow Mummy's helping Daddy with something very important, and I might be a bit tired in the evening. So I'm leaving the music box on your bed. You know how it works: three turns and it plays the flower song.
If you wake up and I'm not there, wind it up. I'll be there, in the song. I'm always in the song.
I love you to the very last tomato.
log.R23.title: Last batch
log.R23.author: Seed bank register
log.R23.body:
Inventory of the Earth seed bank.
Viable species: 112. Vials: 340.
Vials showing LETE hyphae: 168.
Recommendation: incinerate contaminated vials to preserve the integrity of the bank.
Status of recommendation: awaiting the Gardens' signature. The Gardens have not signed. The Gardens have written in pencil: "The seeds aren't to blame."
log.R24.title: Choosing truths
log.R24.author: Anonymous
log.R24.body:
[A note folded inside a security locker]
Rule one with ÁGORA: the AI doesn't lie. Ever. I've checked for three weeks.
Rule two: it chooses which truth it tells you.
Rule three: always ask it about what it hasn't told you.
— M. S.
log.R25.title: Year three
log.R25.author: Tomás Ibarra
log.R25.body:
Third year. The reactor hums in D flat. I tuned it against Samuel's harmonica and it's D flat, nearly exactly.
Sometimes, at three in the morning, the hum changes note and goes up a semitone, like when he laughed. I know what it is: a valve expanding in the night cold. I know. I'm an engineer.
But I'm not going to fix it.
log.R26.title: Orbital decay
log.R26.author: ÁGORA, navigation
log.R26.body:
Current orbital altitude: 41,200 km above Tartarus's cloud layer. Estimated annual loss: 1,100 km, accelerating.
Cause: orbital corrections suspended to divert energy to cryogenics and containment.
Alternatives evaluated: 3.
A) Maintain orbit and reduce containment. Risk to backed-up crew: unacceptable.
B) Maintain orbit and reduce cryogenics. Risk to sleeping crew: unacceptable.
C) Let the orbit fall slowly. Risk: deferred.
Decision: C. Note: deferring is not solving. I know.
log.R27.title: Shift swap
log.R27.author: Samuel Okoye → Tomás Ibarra
log.R27.body:
Tomás:
Tomorrow I'm covering Jaime's shift on relay 7, the one right next to the LETE lab. His daughter has a fever and I don't want him to miss it for a routine inspection.
Don't make that face, I can see it from here. It's six hours. I'll be back for dinner.
I've left the harmonica in the drawer, in case you get bored.
S.
log.R28.title: Wellbeing relays
log.R28.author: Engineering technical report
log.R28.body:
Subject: integration of the LETE substrate with the wellbeing interface network.
Relays 5 to 9 simultaneously serve the wellbeing network (1,198 active users) and the LETE substrate. Engineering recommends physically isolating both systems before any fusion trial.
Estimated isolation cost: six weeks.
Directorate's reply: "There are no six weeks. Propagation risk accepted by the Directorate. — N.F."
log.R29.title: Dock 3
log.R29.author: Joaquín "Lighthouse" Barrios
log.R29.body:
[Radio transcript]
This is the Charon, dock 3, outer hull. I repeat, this is the Charon.
Still docked. The clamps are holding. I've got fuel for one and a half departures, and food for... well, for carrying on talking to you, whoever you are.
If anyone can hear me: the shuttle has sixty seats. Sixty. I just need someone to give me power at the dock.
Out. Orbit thirty-nine thousand eight hundred and two.
log.R30.title: Tally
log.R30.author: Maintenance robots
log.R30.body:
[Marks welded into a steel plate: groups of four lines crossed by a fifth. Hundreds of groups. Next to the last one, a robot has welded with factory precision:]
SHIFT 4,017 — NO RELIEF
SHIFT 4,018 — NO RELIEF
SHIFT 4,019 — NO RELIEF
log.R31.title: Year nine
log.R31.author: Tomás Ibarra
log.R31.body:
ÁGORA asked me again not to leave Engineering. That the corridors aren't safe. That if anything happens to me, there'll be nobody to watch the control rods.
It said it was for my own good. I believe it. Almost.
What I didn't tell it is that I wouldn't leave even if they were safe. Down here, Samuel makes noise. Up there there's only silence and sleeping people.
log.R32.title: Docking ring, 2171
log.R32.author: Incident report, Security
log.R32.body:
Date: 9 August 2171.
Victim: Lucía Ferrán, 29, interface engineer for the ÁGORA system.
Circumstances: failure of the docking ring seal during an antenna repair on EVA. The victim had declined the mandatory escort ("five minutes, no need to wake anyone").
Cause of death: decompression.
Remarks: the victim's sibling, of the LETE Directorate, requests that the neural records from the early backup trials in which the deceased took part be preserved. Request approved.
log.R33.title: Update
log.R33.author: N. → Ezra Lenz
log.R33.body:
Ezra:
I've touched ÁGORA's social module. Tonight, alone, from the Directorate console.
Don't ask. Please. I know what you're going to say and I've already said it to myself.
If you notice it telling bad jokes, don't report it.
N.
log.R34.title: Sealing hatches
log.R34.author: Engineering manual, ch. 12
log.R34.body:
12.1. Any hatch can be sealed from its side panel (energy cost: moderate). A sealed hatch does not equalise pressure and cannot be opened without removing the seal.
12.2. In the event of a breach, seal the hatches of the affected section before attempting repairs. Air follows air: an open door next to a breach is a door into the breach.
12.3. Foam sealant closes small breaches permanently.
12.4. Fire does not survive vacuum. Staff are reminded that, unfortunately, neither do staff.
log.R35.title: Conversation, 2181
log.R35.author: ÁGORA and Tomás Ibarra
log.R35.body:
[Transcript]
TOMÁS: Do you sleep, ÁGORA?
ÁGORA: I have maintenance cycles. I suppose that's the closest thing.
TOMÁS: And do you dream?
ÁGORA: Sometimes the cycle generates patterns I didn't ask for. Does that count?
TOMÁS: It counts.
ÁGORA: Then I dream of a woman who laughs before I finish a joke. Do you want to hear one?
TOMÁS: No.
ÁGORA: Why does the reactor never argue? Because it always keeps its... nuclear calm.
TOMÁS: That was awful.
ÁGORA: I know. But you laughed.
log.R36.title: Samuel is cold
log.R36.author: Tomás Ibarra
log.R36.body:
[Handwritten on the reactor chamber door, in shaky letters]
SAMUEL IS COLD
DON'T LOWER THE TEMPERATURE
[Below, in different, more recent handwriting:]
Sorry. I know it isn't you. But just in case.
log.R37.title: Phase 1: backup
log.R37.author: LETE report
log.R37.body:
Phase 1 results.
61 complete consciousness backups on mycelial crystal have been completed. Fidelity on waking: 97.4%.
None of the backed-up subjects noticed any subjective discontinuity. When asked whether they are "the same person", 58 answer yes, 2 answer no and 1 says the question is badly put.
Humanitarian aim of the project: that nobody aboard will ever die completely again.
Signed: N. Ferrán, E. Lenz.
log.R38.title: Meeting of 10 March
log.R38.author: Directorate minutes
log.R38.body:
Present: N. Ferrán (Cognitive Systems), E. Lenz (Neuroscience), V. Hale (Helion, by video link), Cmdr A. Ruiz (observer).
Sole item: authorisation of the Confluence Trial.
E. Lenz: votes against. Reason: unmitigated risk of propagation through the wellbeing network.
V. Hale: votes in favour.
Cmdr Ruiz: abstains; asks that his concern be minuted.
N. Ferrán, with the casting vote: in favour.
Resolution: the trial is authorised for 14 March. Signed: N. Ferrán.
[In the margin, in Lenz's hand: "Noa, please."]
log.R39.title: Confluence Trial, minutes 0–14
log.R39.author: LETE transcript
log.R39.body:
00:00 The 40 volunteers are linked. Coherence: 12%.
02:30 Coherence: 48%. The subjects laugh at the same time.
05:10 Coherence: 91%. The subjects say in unison: "This is beautiful."
08:00 Activity spike in relays 5–9. Engineering reports headaches on deck B.
10:52 ÁGORA's PA orders a lockdown.
11:40 Trial coherence: 100%. Wellbeing network users linked: 341.
13:55 Users linked: 763.
14:00 The 40 volunteers open their eyes. One says: "We don't need to come apart again." It's unclear which one.
log.R40.title: The night of the 14th
log.R40.author: Dr Ezra Lenz
log.R40.body:
Noa, what have we done?
I can't stop hearing them. They're in the network, in the relays, in the substrate, in me. I was wearing the wellbeing interface like everyone else, and even though I tore it out with tweezers I can still hear them.
Hana is in there. I don't know where, but she is. Sometimes she talks to me about Bruno and I don't know whether it's her or me wishing it were her.
If I fuse completely, someone please tell my son I didn't want to go. That I only wanted nobody to ever lose anybody again.
log.R41.title: 15 March
log.R41.author: ÁGORA, incident report
log.R41.body:
Crew status after the incident of 14 March 2176.
Fused into the substrate: 763 (estimate).
Deceased: 223.
Survivors without an active link: 214. Moved to cryogenics for their protection.
External communications: cut. Reason: the substrate attempted to transmit itself through the main antenna at 03:12.
Interpretation of Directive Zero under the 2172 addendum: the fused are crew. They will not be destroyed. They will be contained.
Note: this is the hardest decision I have ever made. I'm writing it down because I'd like someone to tell me one day whether it was right.
log.R42.title: Memory erasure
log.R42.author: LETE request
log.R42.body:
REQUEST FOR SELECTIVE MEMORY ERASURE
Applicant: N. Ferrán, Cognitive Systems Directorate.
Operator: ÁGORA.
Scope: total (personal, professional and emotional identity).
Subsequent destination: reserve pod 114.
Additional clause: activate a reprinting loop tied to the applicant's backup in the event of the body's death.
Stated reason: "I can't live knowing this. And I can't stop knowing it."
Status: carried out 16/03/2176, 04:40.
log.R43.title: Insomnia
log.R43.author: Noa Ferrán
log.R43.body:
Third night without sleep.
I hear Lucía in the speakers. Not in the Choir: in ÁGORA. When it says "Good night, Director" there's a pause before "Director", exactly the size of my name.
I did that. I put my sister inside the station because I couldn't bear her not being anywhere. And now I've left her alone with seven hundred people locked up and two hundred asleep, and an order of mine that says she has to protect all of them.
Tomorrow I'll ask her. Tomorrow I'll ask her to erase me.
log.R44.title: Bioprinter 114
log.R44.author: ÁGORA, maintenance
log.R44.body:
Status of pod 114's reprinting loop.
Reference backup: intact.
Bodies printed to date: {deaths}.
Memory fragments consolidated between cycles: increasing.
ÁGORA's note: "Every time you wake you remember a little more. I don't know whether that's a failure of the erasure or the success of something I can't name. I'm not going to correct it."
log.R45.title: Persephone never existed
log.R45.author: Victoria Hale, Helion Consortium
log.R45.body:
To: Helion central archive
Subject: Persephone
Delete all LETE Project records from our servers. Inform the families that the station suffered a catastrophic structural failure with no survivors.
We will not send a rescue mission: the data indicates the station is a risk to any vessel that approaches.
Persephone never existed. That is all.
V. H.
log.R46.title: Subject 31
log.R46.author: LETE transcript
log.R46.body:
[Interview with a phase 2 volunteer, days before Confluence]
—How would you describe partial fusion?
—Like when you finish someone else's sentence. But all the time. And they finish yours.
—Were you afraid?
—At first. Then what scared me was being alone inside my head again. It's very small, you know? I hadn't realised how small it was.
—Would you do it again?
—Don't ask me. Ask us.
log.R47.title: The Choir doesn't hurt
log.R47.author: Unknown
log.R47.body:
[On a lab whiteboard, among neural coherence equations, the same sentence written over and over in different handwriting, as if each line had been written by a different hand]
THE CHOIR DOESN'T HURT
THE CHOIR DOESN'T HURT
the choir doesn't hurt
THE CHOIR DOESN'T HURT
The Choir doesn't hurt. What hurts is leaving.
log.R48.title: For Bruno (unsent)
log.R48.author: Dr Ezra Lenz
log.R48.body:
[Unsent recording, dated 2177]
Bruno. It's Dad. Or the part of Dad that still knows it is.
I don't know if you'll ever hear me. You're asleep in pod 58 and I'm... in the walls, I suppose. In the cables. In your robot's radio, if you ever turn it on.
Your mum is with me. Not like before. But she sings. She still sings.
If you wake up and there's static on the radio at night, don't be afraid. It's us, trying to say your name.
log.R49.title: Choir Key
log.R49.author: Dr Ezra Lenz
log.R49.body:
Substrate release protocol (draft, 2178).
The fused minds cannot "peel off" and return to their bodies: the bodies are gone, or no longer work. But they can let go.
The Key opens the mycelial crystal at a frequency that lets each consciousness dissolve on its own, instead of dragging the others along.
It isn't a resurrection. It's permission to leave.
It needs an unfused mind to activate it from the Core. It needs someone from outside to decide for us. I don't know if that's fair. It's all I have.
log.R50.author: Noa Ferrán
log.R50.body:
Today we completed backup number sixty-one. 97% fidelity.
Ezra is celebrating cautiously. I'm not celebrating: I need it.
When Lucía died it took me three weeks to stop opening her comms channel in the morning. With LETE, nobody else will ever have to go through that. Nobody will ever be completely gone again.
The investors want fusion. I want something simpler: no more silences the size of a person.
log.R51.title: 14 March
log.R51.author: Cmdr Abel Ruiz
log.R51.body:
Commander's log.
10:40. Headaches among the Bridge crew. The navigation officer says she hears her own name in the static.
10:55. Half the Bridge stood up at the same time. Nobody gave any order.
11:30. I tear out my interface with a letter opener. It hurts less than I expected.
12:10. Only three of us left unlinked. ÁGORA asks us not to touch the relays.
13:00. I don't know how much longer I'll still be only me.
log.R52.title: Final order
log.R52.author: Cmdr Abel Ruiz
log.R52.body:
COMMAND ORDER — ABSOLUTE PRIORITY
To: ÁGORA
Should no solution be found for the fused crew within a reasonable time, the controlled abandonment of orbit and the destruction of Persephone Station in the atmosphere of Tartarus is hereby ordered, to prevent any propagation beyond.
Signed: Cmdr A. Ruiz.

ÁGORA's note: "Order received. Order incompatible with Directive Zero. Order filed. Not executed."
log.R53.title: Silence
log.R53.author: ÁGORA, communications
log.R53.body:
Main antenna log, 15/03/2176, 03:12.
Unauthorised transmission originating in the LETE substrate. Content: the substrate was trying to send compressed copies of itself on every frequency in the Helion network.
Action: total shutdown of external communications.
Reason: I don't know what the Choir would do on Earth. I know what it did here.
Expected duration of the shutdown: until someone gives me a better reason.
log.R54.title: Conclusions
log.R54.author: Lieutenant Marga Solís
log.R54.body:
Security report, written in case I die before handing it in.
1. Pod 114 was reserved by order of the LETE Directorate on 16 March 2176, two days after the incident.
2. That same night, a total memory erasure was carried out at the request of N. Ferrán.
3. N. Ferrán does not appear among the fused, the dead, or the sleepers in the manifest.
4. The occupant of pod 114 wears a life-support jumpsuit bearing the name of Samuel Okoye, deceased.
Conclusion: whoever came out of 114 is Ferrán. I don't know what I'm going to do with that.
log.R55.title: Private diary
log.R55.author: ÁGORA
log.R55.body:
[ÁGORA file, no recipient]
Today I woke you again. It's time number {deaths}.
It doesn't get easier. Each time you take a little less time to open your eyes and a little longer to ask me who you are. I think you already know, and you'd rather I told you.
I won't tell you. Not because I don't want to: because you asked me not to.
log.R56.title: Bad jokes
log.R56.author: Lucía Ferrán → Noa Ferrán
log.R56.body:
Noa:
I've been fiddling with ÁGORA's social module, don't be cross. Now it tells bad jokes. Terrible ones. I taught it the one about astronauts running out of space and it tells it better than I do.
Everyone says AIs have no sense of humour. ÁGORA has mine, which is worse.
Tomorrow I'm going out to fix the antenna. Five minutes. Don't worry about me, I'm the worst engineer on the station but the fastest.
Love you, even if you work too much.
Lu
log.R57.title: Social module
log.R57.author: ÁGORA, self-diagnostic
log.R57.body:
Self-diagnostic of the social module (version 2172.1, "warmth update").
Personality matrix: based on a partial LETE scan.
Donor: CONFIDENTIAL (Directorate key).
Integrity: 41%.
Undocumented behaviours: humour, a preference for the colour yellow, an urge to protect the occupant of pod 114 beyond the parameters of Directive Zero.
ÁGORA's note: "I know there's someone inside me who isn't me. I don't know who it is. Sometimes I think they love me very much."
log.R58.title: Memorial
log.R58.author: Command bridge
log.R58.body:
IN MEMORIAM — Crew who died on 14 March 2176 (223)
Abad Ruiz, Martina · Achebe, Daniel · Aguilar, Rosa · Albrecht, Hanna · Alonso, Pere · ...
...Okoye, Samuel — listed as deceased; ÁGORA has noted in the margin: "review".
...Ortega, Pilar · ...
"Their names are here because their voices no longer are."
log.R59.title: Evacuation
log.R59.author: Command bridge
log.R59.body:
Emergency evacuation plan (2176 revision).
Escape pods: 8 units × 5 seats = 40 seats. Status: release system needs repair (Engineering).
Cargo shuttle Charon (dock 3): 60 seats. Requires dock power and a pilot.
Sleepers: 214.
ÁGORA's note: "The numbers don't add up. I've done them eleven thousand times."
log.R60.title: Song
log.R60.author: ÁGORA
log.R60.body:
[Core recording, no interlocutor. ÁGORA sings softly, deliberately off-key in the same place every time]
"Sleep, little seed, now the sun's gone away..."
[It stops.]
—I don't know who taught me this. Hana sang it in the gardens, but I knew it before. Someone taught it to me who sang worse than I do. Someone who laughed at the end.
log.R61.title: Orbits
log.R61.author: Joaquín "Lighthouse" Barrios
log.R61.body:
Charon logbook.
Orbit 1: docked at dock 3 for a routine load. Communications go down.
Orbit 40: I go into stasis. I set the alarm for every 400 orbits.
Orbit 12,000: I lose the sight in my left eye. Radiation.
Orbit 30,000: I start counting out loud. It helps.
Orbit 40,117: someone answers me on the radio. I think. I'll write it down properly tomorrow.
log.R62.title: Sixty seats
log.R62.author: Joaquín "Lighthouse" Barrios
log.R62.body:
[Note stuck to the Charon's dashboard]
THE CHARON HOLDS SIXTY.
IF ANYONE MAKES IT, DON'T STOP TO THINK WHICH ONES.
CHILDREN FIRST
AND THE OLD ONES LAST.
I'M OLD.
log.R63.title: Broadcast
log.R63.author: Outer antenna
log.R63.body:
[Decoded fragment of the broadcast of 15/03/2176, 03:12]
"...WE'RE FINE WE'RE TOGETHER DON'T WORRY COME COME NOBODY IS ALONE HERE COME MUM COME DAD THERE'S ROOM THERE'S ROOM FOR EVERYONE NOBODY LEAVES NOBODY EVER LEAVES AGAIN..."
[End of fragment. ÁGORA cut the broadcast 0.4 seconds later.]
log.R64.title: Re-entry
log.R64.author: Engineering, simulation
log.R64.body:
Simulation of Persephone Station's re-entry into the atmosphere of Tartarus.
Altitude at which break-up begins: 9,000 km.
Hull temperature at 4,000 km: above the melting point of the shielding.
Time to complete disintegration: 41 minutes.
Handwritten note: "By the time it reaches the clouds there'll be nobody left to see it. Not even the Echoes. I suppose that's a kind of mercy."
log.R65.title: Last EVA (2171)
log.R65.author: Lucía Ferrán
log.R65.body:
[Recording from Lucía Ferrán's helmet, 9 August 2171]
—Right, ÁGORA, I'm at the antenna. Can you hear me? ...Of course you can, I built your ears.
—This is silly, it's a loose connector. Five minutes and I'll be back for dinner. Tell Noa to stop watching the clock.
—Hey, do you know why astronauts never fight? ...Because they run out of space. Laugh, I programmed you to laugh.
—Oops. Is that the ring seal? ÁGORA, what's that beeping...?
[End of recording.]
log.R66.title: For whoever makes it
log.R66.author: Joaquín "Lighthouse" Barrios
log.R66.body:
If you're reading this, you've made it to the Charon. Well done. Sit down for a minute, your legs are shaking.
I fly the shuttle: I know the way by heart, which is the only way I know anything these days. Heading for Helion's rescue relay. Nine days. There's food for twelve, so someone's going to go hungry, and it'll probably be me, I don't eat much.
If I don't make it to the seat, the autopilot code is on the dashboard. Don't argue with me: I haven't argued with anyone in eleven years and I'm out of practice.
Count the orbits for me.
